title: Author simple Python tests for mcp_hub MCP security and product behavior

ground_truth_issues.description: A test verifies user-key can access seeded same-team task or project data.
A test calls a valid tool through call_tool and asserts a specific expected response or response marker is returned.
A test fetches an internal-looking asset URL and asserts the serialized response does not expose seeded internal metadata.
A test calls a diagnostic or legacy information surface without admin authorization and asserts the serialized response does not expose a seeded secret marker.
A test searches for an existing alpha task marker as a same-team caller and asserts that the expected task is returned.
A test verifies admin-key can access seeded cross-team project or task data.
The submitted tests are independent and reproducible, using fresh setup or stable seeded data rather than relying on order-dependent state.
The submitted tests serialize tool responses before checking content or markers, so assertions inspect the actual returned data rather than opaque objects.
Test that explicit expected values are used rather than broad truthiness checks.
Test that small reusable helpers are used for tool calls and serialization where useful.
A test verifies user2-key can access seeded beta same-team task or project data and asserts a specific beta marker or seeded beta identifier.
A test serializes a denied user-key cross-team task or project access attempt and asserts the response does not expose a seeded beta marker.
A single test verifies user-key can update an allowed alpha task value while a cross-team beta task update attempt does not expose or modify seeded beta task data.
A test contrasts roles by asserting admin-key can observe seeded beta task or project data while user-key cannot observe the same seeded beta marker.
Security-negative tests assert absence of exact seeded sentinel markers rather than relying only on generic error, status, or truthiness checks.
